To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the maximum and minimum sizes of zones are both bounded by the number of peers, and that the maximum zone size is bounded from above by the number of nodes in the network.

the maximum zone size of consistent hashing is O(n1/2), that this is tight for the case of random node join, that it is possible to achieve a maximum zone size that is O(log n), and that this can be done without any prior knowledge about the peer space.

(1) a simple random sampling of the peer-space is the best possible zone-balancing strategy in the asymptotic limit and (2) the asymptotic zone size of a consistent-hashing DHT is independent of its node degree and only depends on the number of peers in the system and the number of nodes in the routing table.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the impact of different sampling strategies on the resulting zone sizes? What is the asymptotic behavior of zone size distributions? What is the impact on the load balancing of the choice of the initial sampling size?

the following questions: What is the maximum and minimum possible zone size for consistent hashing? What is the impact of initial sampling on zone sizes? What are the performance limitations of consistent-hashing-based peer-join mechanisms? What are the implications of these limitations for the design of DHTs based on consistent hashing?
the following question: How does the initial sampling of peer space affect the performance of consistent hashing?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best zone-balancing method depends on the application scenario.
the de Bruijn graph has a very good load balancing property.
the de Bruijn graph with a random node join is a good candidate for a DHT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a large class of DHTs, the zone-balancing decisions taken at the beginning of the system's lifetime have a major impact on the system's performance.

, for the de Bruijn graph, a random initial sampling of the node space is the best way to achieve zone-balancing, and that the performance of the resulting system is very close to that of a perfect balanced system.
the asymptotic behavior of the various peer-joining mechanisms is very different.
The main takeaway from our work is that
zone balancing during the initial sampling phase is crucial for the performance of consistent hashing, and that a zone size of 1 is the worst-case scenario for the load-balancing performance.
the asymptotic performance of consistent hashing is highly sensitive to the initial sampling of zone boundaries.
the zone size distribution of consistent hashing depends on the initial sampling method.
